summary: Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She has held posts as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011).
Nang Dzé Drubpé Dorjé was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Nanigopal Majumdar (1897–1938) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. He served as a Superintendent in the Archaeological Survey of India (1931) and as Superintendent of the Archæological Section at the Indian Museum, Kolkata (attested 1939).
Nantu Shaw is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied as a Visiting Scholar at Stony Brook University under doctoral supervisor Sthaneshwar Timalsina (attested 2026).

Naoji Okuyama (b. 1956) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1980–1985), where he was an assistant and lecturer (~1985–1993), before becoming a professor at Koyasan University (~1997).
Naoki Nabeshima specializes in Buddhist studies. He founded and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2004).

Naoko Nishimura is an Indologist and linguist who earned a PhD at Tohoku University (1993–2002) studying under Toshifumi Goto, Hirofumi Isoda, and Shinkan Murakami. She has served as a specialized researcher at Tohoku University (attested 2026).

Naomi Appleton works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. After earning a D.Phil. at Oxford under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner, she was a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Cardiff and became Professor and Co-Director at Edinburgh.
Naomi Worth works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Virginia and held a post there (attested 2018).
Naomichi Nakada (b. 1928) is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied under doctoral supervisor Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale and under Ram Chandra Pandeya.

Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Tokyo and Oxford. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960), professor at Keio University (1960), and director of Toyo Bunko (1974).
Naoya Funahashi (b. 1937) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held positions with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and at Otani University (attested 1981).

Narada Maha Thera (1898–1983) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who was educated at St. Benedict's College and University College, Colombo. He served as Superior at Vajiraramaya Temple (~1955–1983).

Narayan Hemandas Samtani (1924–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi (1957–1961) under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale and taught Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1958–1984).

Narayana Shastri Khiste was an Indology scholar who served as Librarian (अध्यक्ष) at the Sarasvati Bhavana Library (attested 1932) and as Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1950).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya (1934–2001) was a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology who held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from circa 1967 to 1999.

Narendrachandra Bhattacharyya was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as General Editor for the Calcutta Sanskrit Series (attested 1936) and as a Pandit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).

Naresh Keerthi specializes in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the National Institute of Advanced Studies (attested 2015–2017), the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2018–2021), and became an Assistant Professor at Ashoka University in 2021.

Nariaki Nakazato (b. 1946) is an Indologist and historian who studied at Tokyo and Calcutta. He held appointments at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, Toyo Bunko, Kobe University, and served as Professor at the University of Tokyo (~1994–2011).
Narimoto Tamayama (1916–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1974 and 1988).
